messages:
alex chen: Heads-up — our leak scanner flagged a partner ingest containing wrapped KMS ciphertext and a truncated service-account email. Payloads reference `projects/infra-ops/locations/global/keyRings/ring-1/cryptoKeys/serve-key`. Not public yet but we should treat as breached. :rotating_light:

security-bot: [auto-alert] detector=creds-scrape severity=high rule_id=ks-037 path=partner-logs/2026-03-20-*.log matches=3

zia patel: Can we confirm whether the ciphertext is raw KMS ciphertext or a Vault-wrapped payload? If it's KMS directly we need a KMS rekey + rewrap. If Vault-wrapped we rotate the transit key + reissue wrapped secrets.

alex chen: I pulled the snippet — looks like KMS ciphertext blob (base64) with a nearby svcacc email. Example log line: `{"event":"upload","user":"svc-data-ingest@partner.com","object":"obj.json","payload":"CiQA...base64..."}`. No vault metadata in the line.

maya singh: Ok — treat as KMS key exposure vector. Immediate actions: 1) scope down key IAM (remove all non-essential members), 2) enable audit log forwarding for Cloud KMS and Storage to sec-logs-retention, 3) schedule key rewrap and service-account rotations. I can drive the runbook.

lee wong: For RBAC: who currently has cryptokeyEncrypterDecrypter on serve-key? I can run a quick IAM diff and remove partner/beta roles. Also we should add a temporary conditional binding (expires in 12h) for critical infra.

alex chen: Lee — thanks. If you can post the diff here we'll approve. I also want to rotate any long-lived service tokens that reference that svcacc email. Maya — what's your ETA for the runbook?

maya singh: Drafting now. ETA 30m for a minimal step list and owners. High-level steps I plan to include:
- Lockdown: remove non-prod members from key IAM, mark key as 'do-not-use' in routing rules.
- Audit: export KMS & Storage logs for the last 30d, snapshot partner buckets.
- Rotate keys: create new key version + rewrap ciphertext where possible.
- Reissue creds: create ephemeral service accounts where we can, rotate long-lived tokens, revoke old keys.
- Verify: smoke tests for model-serving and ingestion pipelines.
- Postmortem: timeline + leakage source analysis.

zia patel: Couple of technical notes: rewrapping ciphertext in-place isn't always feasible — you must decrypt then re-encrypt with the new key version. For files we don't control (partner buckets) we may need partner cooperation or re-ingest from source. Also enable CMEK audit logs and set log-based alerts for use of the old key.

lee wong: IAM diff: I removed `group:partner-ingest@partners` binding from serve-key and revoked a couple of service accounts that matched the leaked pattern. Pasted output: ```
IAM changes applied:
- roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter: removed member=group:partner-ingest@partners
- roles/cloudkms.viewer: removed member=serviceAccount:old-ingest@redwood-infer.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

alex chen: Nice. @maya can you add a step to rotate any Vault transit keys that might have been used to wrap prep pipelines? Even though we saw KMS, better to be thorough.

maya singh: Added. Also proposing a short maintenance window 2h from now to perform rekeys & token rotations. Need opt-in from infra owners. Calling out owners: @lee (IAM), @alex (partner coord + token listing), @zia (audit + rewrap scripts).

zia patel: I'll run a quick script to list blobs that likely contain ciphertext patterns and produce a prioritized list. Script snippet I plan to run: ```bash
gsutil ls gs://partner-bucket/** | xargs -n1 -P8 bash -c 'gsutil cat "$0" | grep -E "[A-Za-z0-9+/]{60,}" && echo "$0"'
```
Sharing results in 20m.

security-bot: [workflow] created incident ticket INC-2026-0423 and attached initial alert. Runbook template: /playbooks/secure-rotate-v2.

lee wong: Quick Q on audit: do we have KMS cryptoKeyDecrypted/Encrypted events aggregated in a central SIEM? If not, we need to forward before the rekey so we can validate old-key usage after rotation.

maya singh: We do forward to sec-logs-retention but retention is short. I'll ask SRE to snapshot logs to a longer-term bucket and add a log sink for the SIEM. Zia — include required log filters in your export.

alex chen: I'll message the partner lead to freeze ingestion and request access to re-ingest raw sources if needed. Also starting a quick token sweep: searching GitHub/CI artifacts for the svcacc email and any long-lived keys.

zia patel: Results: found 12 objects with base64-like blobs and 2 CI runs that referenced the svcacc. I'm marking those high-priority for re-ingest/rotation.

maya singh: Owners confirmed. We start the maintenance window at 4990015000 (approx 45m). Steps will be run in this order: IAM lockdown -> log snapshot -> key new-version creation -> decrypt/rewrap controlled data -> token revocation -> smoke tests -> reopen. Post those who executed commands here.

lee wong: I'll be on for the window. Will keep diffs recorded. :thumbsup:

alex chen: I'll coordinate partner comms and token sweep.

security-bot: [update] INC-2026-0423 status=investigating severity=high assignees=alex chen,maya singh,lee wong

maya singh: Closing note: after rotation we should enable stricter key policies (no direct project-level bindings for partners), add KMS key usage quotas, and require ephemeral tokens for partner ingest. Will draft policy change PR.

alex chen: Thanks all. We'll post a short postmortem and follow-on policy PR after the incident is contained. :spiral_notepad:
